definition: to delay or block by creating an obstacle
memoryTip: Im-pede: put something in the path of the feet — slow progress.
correctPassage: Construction along the highway will impede delivery trucks until the detour opens next month.
wrongPassages: Additional funding will impede the research team’s ability to finish the study on schedule.
The new software is designed to impede workflow by automating the most time-consuming steps.
Mentors impede first-year students by helping them navigate registration and course selection.

definition: to gather information bit by bit from various sources
memoryTip: Farmers glean leftover grain — pick up scraps of info the same way.
correctPassage: From scattered field notes, the biologist could glean how the bird population had shifted over decades.
wrongPassages: She chose to glean the entire archive in a single uninterrupted afternoon of reading.
Investigators gleaned the missing motive by inventing details no witness had supplied.
Administrators chose to glean the controversial passage by deleting it from the final report.

definition: lasting only a very short time
memoryTip: Ephemera once meant “for a day” — here today, gone tomorrow.
correctPassage: The desert bloom is ephemeral, vanishing within days once the rains end.
wrongPassages: Stone monuments are ephemeral because they outlast the civilizations that raised them.
Their ephemeral collaboration has produced books together for more than thirty years.
He filed the ephemeral records in a permanent archive meant to preserve them indefinitely.

memoryTip: In scattered spots — now and then, not on a steady schedule.
correctPassage: The rare bird appears only sporadically along this stretch of coast.
wrongPassages: The factory whistle blew sporadically at the same minute every morning without fail.
She practiced sporadically: two hours each day for six months without missing a session.
Trains arrived sporadically according to a published timetable that never varied.

definition: filled with something undesirable; tense with risk
memoryTip: Freighted with trouble — loaded down with tension or danger.
correctPassage: The negotiations were fraught with misunderstandings from the first meeting.
wrongPassages: Their vacation was fraught with calm beaches and uninterrupted sleep.
The simple recipe was fraught with only three ingredients and one pan.
He found the empty hallway fraught with silence and free of any tension.
